title: Control-plane fallback protocols for rolling upgrades in Dedicated/Private clusters
creator: Marco Alvarez
description: Problem: Rolling upgrades to control-plane components in Dedicated and Private deployments have caused tenant-visible latency spikes and cascading failures when kernel selection and KV-cache priming are interrupted. We need a standardized fallback protocol that ensures zero-or-minimal customer impact during upgrades by combining SLO-driven admission control, multi-region consensus failover, and tiered circuit breakers/load-shedding. Goal: design and implement a control-plane quarantine and fallback system that isolates upgrade-affected instances, maintains per-tenant SLO guarantees where possible, and gracefully degrades non-critical traffic to preserve availability for critical tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Control-plane can mark an upgrade-affected node group as 'quarantined' without reconfiguring tenant routes manually
Requests routed away from quarantined nodes within 30s and failover latency to alternate region < 200ms for cross-region path (where region TTL allows)
SLO adherence: critical tenant P99 latency increase < 15% during a rolling upgrade in the same region, and error rate increase < 0.5%
Circuit breaker tiers implemented: per-tenant, per-route, and global. Tiers trigger progressive load-shedding based on SLO burn rate and capacity signals
Automated rollback trigger that will pause the upgrade and promote a last-known-good control-plane snapshot if > 5% of tenants cross emergency SLOs within a 10-minute window
Runbook and automated Playbook activities validated in canary private deployments and one Dedicated cluster before wide rollout
implementation_steps: Design quarantine marker and node-group label semantics in control-plane API (owner: infra-runtime)
Add SLO budget calculator in the routing layer that consumes tenant SLO and current burn-rate metrics (owner: routing-service)
Implement multi-tier circuit breaker system with explicit thresholds: soft degrade, aggressive shed, emergency stop (owner: serving-runtime)
Extend multi-region failover coordinator to support voting with tenant-priority weights and config-driven region-preference lists (owner: multi-region)
Create admission-control webhook for Dedicated/Private control-plane that rejects or queues non-critical requests when capacity headroom < X% (owner: private-ops)
Wire observability: new dashboards, traces, and alert rules for quarantine events and SLO burn (owner: observability)
QA: simulate rolling upgrade scenarios with chaos tests that flip node states and measure SLOs per-tenant (owner: reliability-test)
Documentation: update runbooks, console UI hints, and API docs for quarantine and fallback controls (owner: docs)
Release: staged rollout starting in staging -> canary private -> one Dedicated region -> global
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag behind 'cp-quarantine' in staging clusters. Smoke tests only.
Phase 1: Canary: enable in one Private customer-resembling cluster with synthetic traffic templates for 72 hours
Phase 2: Dedicated canary: enable in a low-risk Dedicated shard during a maintenance window; monitor SLOs for 1 week
Phase 3: Gradual ramp: enable across remaining Dedicated clusters with incremental tenant throttling to validate fallback behavior
Phase 4: GA: enable for all Private deployments and surface controls in Console with opt-in/out for enterprise customers
test_plan: Unit tests for quarantine markers, CB logic, and admission-control webhook
Integration tests that verify routing respects quarantined node groups across regions
Chaos tests: orchestrate node churn during upgrade and assert SLO thresholds for a set of critical tenants
Load tests: ensure circuit breaker tiers reduce cost and maintain availability under 30%, 60%, and 90% simulated load spikes
DR test: simulate full region failure and validate multi-region failover coordinator elects target region within configured quiesce window
metrics: Reroute latency histogram (us) for quarantined vs non-quarantined paths
Circuit breaker activation counts per tier
Customer-facing error rate and P99 latency by tenant during upgrades
